correctness.rationale: In a complete multipartite graph, a positive vertex has a positive neighbor exactly when another part contains a positive label, and a zero in part \(V_i\) has a \(2\)-neighbor exactly when a 2 occurs outside \(V_i\). These equivalences prove the structural criterion. The polynomial partitions labelings into the mutually exclusive cases of \(2\)-labels in at least two parts, exactly one part, or no parts. The minimum formula follows by optimizing each case. Brute-force verification through order 9 independently checks the literal graph definition, criterion, every polynomial coefficient, and the minimum.

value.rationale: Total Roman domination is an established domination invariant, and complete multipartite graphs are a canonical structured family. The theorem classifies every feasible labeling and gives the exact weight distribution, strictly more information than a minimum-value formula. The enumerator supports exact counts of optimal and nonoptimal strategies and immediate probabilistic or coefficient questions, while the structural criterion is simple enough to be reusable.
